turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Hello, I'm Maya. I am a first-year physics student.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: I'm Jordan. I study physics too, and I usually study at the library.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: My mathematics class begins at nine on Monday. What time does your class begin?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: At ten on Monday. We can review our notes after class.

questions.prompt: What subject do both students study?
questions.feedback: Both students say that they study physics.

questions.prompt: When does Maya's mathematics class begin on Monday?
questions.feedback: Maya says that her mathematics class starts at nine on Monday.

pronunciation.phrase: I study physics too, and I usually study at the library.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the unstressed function words in 'I study physics too' and keep the final /s/ sound in physics.

turns.speaker: Instructor
turns.text: Welcome to the department. The laboratory introduction is on Thursday at two in Lab 3.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Do we need to bring any equipment?

turns.speaker: Instructor
turns.text: No. Please bring your student card and a notebook. You do not need laboratory equipment for this introduction.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Thank you. I will write down the time and room.

questions.prompt: Where is the Thursday introduction?
questions.feedback: The instructor identifies Lab 3.

questions.prompt: What should students bring?
options: A student card and a notebook
A laboratory coat and a laser
accepted: A student card and a notebook
questions.feedback: The instructor asks for a student card and a notebook, not laboratory equipment.

pronunciation.phrase: Please bring your student card and a notebook.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the polite sentence rhythm and make the final /d/ in card audible.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: These are illustrative values from our digital model, not real measurements.

turns.speaker: Amina
turns.text: Sample A has a length of 0.35 m. Sample B has a mass of 0.80 kg.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Good. What is the time interval for Sample C?

turns.speaker: Amina
turns.text: It is 12.5 s. I will keep a space before each unit symbol.

questions.prompt: What quantity does Sample B represent?
questions.feedback: Sample B is stated as a mass of 0.80 kg.

questions.prompt: What time interval is given for Sample C?
questions.feedback: The simulated time interval is 12.5 seconds.

pronunciation.phrase: Sample B has a mass of 0.80 kg.
pronunciation.focus: Practise saying 'zero point eight zero kilograms' while keeping the written unit symbol kg unchanged.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Listen to the difference between thirteen and thirty.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Thirteen means 13. Thirty means 30.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Exactly. Now read 0.05 aloud.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Zero point zero five. The digits after the decimal point are read separately.

questions.prompt: Which number means thirty?
questions.feedback: Thirty is the number 30; thirteen is 13.

questions.prompt: How is 0.05 read aloud?
questions.feedback: The student correctly reads the two decimal digits separately.

pronunciation.phrase: Thirteen means 13. Thirty means 30.
pronunciation.focus: Pay attention to the different stress patterns in 'thirteen' and 'thirty' in American English.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: In the virtual room, there is a ruler to the left of the timer.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Where is the notebook?

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: It is under the ruler. There are two labels next to the timer.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I can describe the layout without touching real apparatus.

questions.prompt: Where is the ruler relative to the timer?
questions.feedback: Leila puts the ruler to the left of the timer in the virtual room.

questions.prompt: How many labels are next to the timer?
questions.feedback: The fictional arrangement has two labels beside the timer.

pronunciation.phrase: There are two labels next to the timer.
pronunciation.focus: Contrast 'there are' with 'there is' and pronounce the plural /z/ in labels.

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: Look at the picture of our storage shelf. Box A is on the top shelf.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Is Box B next to Box A?

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: No. Box B is below Box A, on the lower shelf. The blue card is between two books.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I see. These are labels in a diagram, not real lab instructions.

questions.prompt: Which box is on the lower shelf?
questions.feedback: Box B is below Box A on the lower shelf.

questions.prompt: Where is the blue card?
questions.feedback: The guide states that the blue card is between two books.

pronunciation.phrase: Box B is below Box A, on the lower shelf.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the /b/ at the start of Box and below, and pause naturally at the comma.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: The virtual cart usually moves from left to right in our examples.

turns.speaker: Mila
turns.text: What is it doing right now?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: It is moving to the right, but it is slowing down.

turns.speaker: Mila
turns.text: So 'usually moves' is a routine, and 'is slowing down' describes now.

questions.prompt: Which expression describes the present action?
questions.feedback: 'Is slowing down' is present continuous for an action in progress.

questions.prompt: What direction is the cart moving now?
questions.feedback: Noah explicitly says that the virtual cart is moving to the right.

pronunciation.phrase: It is moving to the right, but it is slowing down.
pronunciation.focus: Practise linking 'it is' and keep the /ŋ/ sound at the end of moving.

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: The simulation usually starts with a stationary wheel.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Now the wheel is rotating slowly.

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: Yes, and the blue marker is moving around the center.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: I can describe the motion, but the picture does not give me a numerical angular speed.

questions.prompt: What is the wheel doing now?
questions.feedback: The student says the wheel is rotating slowly.

questions.prompt: Does the picture give a numerical angular speed?
questions.feedback: The student explicitly says no numerical angular speed is provided.

pronunciation.phrase: Now the wheel is rotating slowly.
pronunciation.focus: Practise /w/ in wheel and the primary stress in rotating.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: In this fictional comparison, Cable X is 60 cm long and Cable Y is 80 cm long.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Cable Y is longer than Cable X.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: By how much?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: By 20 cm. This says nothing about how accurate the lengths are.

questions.prompt: Which cable is longer?
questions.feedback: Cable Y is 80 cm while Cable X is 60 cm.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the cable lengths?
questions.feedback: Subtracting 60 cm from 80 cm gives 20 cm.

pronunciation.phrase: Cable Y is longer than Cable X.
pronunciation.focus: Notice the ending /ər/ in longer in American English.

turns.speaker: Aya
turns.text: In the virtual image, Spring A stretches 4 cm and Spring B stretches 6 cm.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: So Spring B stretches more than Spring A.

turns.speaker: Aya
turns.text: Yes. We can compare these simulated stretches.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: But they do not tell us whether a real instrument is accurate.

questions.prompt: How far does Spring A stretch in the model?
questions.feedback: The simulated stretch of Spring A is 4 cm.

questions.prompt: Which statement is supported?
questions.feedback: The dialogue gives 6 cm for B and 4 cm for A.

pronunciation.phrase: Spring B stretches more than Spring A.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the consonant cluster in stretches and the comparative phrase 'more than'.

turns.speaker: Instructor
turns.text: In this classroom example, you must ask before changing a power-supply setting.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Can I change it without approval?

turns.speaker: Instructor
turns.text: No. You must not change it without the instructor's permission.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: I should read the rules carefully before the activity.

questions.prompt: What must students do before changing a setting?
questions.feedback: The fictional rule requires instructor permission before any change.

questions.prompt: What does 'must not' mean here?
questions.feedback: Must not expresses prohibition, not advice.

pronunciation.phrase: You must not change it without the instructor's permission.
pronunciation.focus: Stress 'not' when expressing a prohibition. Follow actual local laboratory rules in real situations.

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: This is a language exercise about a fictional optics notice.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: What does the warning say?

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: It says you must never look directly into a laser beam. Do not point it toward people.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: If I do not understand the instructions, I should ask an instructor.

questions.prompt: What does the fictional notice prohibit?
options: Looking directly into a laser beam
accepted: Looking directly into a laser beam
questions.feedback: The notice forbids looking directly into a laser beam.

questions.prompt: What should a student do if the instructions are unclear?
questions.feedback: The student says to ask the instructor for clarification.

pronunciation.phrase: If I do not understand the instructions, I should ask an instructor.
pronunciation.focus: Practise clear sentence stress on 'do not' and 'ask'.

turns.speaker: Amir
turns.text: Yesterday we opened the virtual pendulum model.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: I checked the unit labels and recorded a time interval of 2.5 s.

turns.speaker: Amir
turns.text: Then I wrote a note about the displayed result.

turns.speaker: Nina
turns.text: We did not perform a physical pendulum experiment.

questions.prompt: What time interval did Nina record?
questions.feedback: Nina reports a displayed time interval of 2.5 s.

questions.prompt: Which irregular past-tense verb does Amir use?
questions.feedback: Wrote is the past tense of write.

pronunciation.phrase: I checked the unit labels and recorded a time interval of 2.5 s.
pronunciation.focus: Compare the /t/ at the end of checked with the /ɪd/ ending of recorded.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: What did you do after the digital trial?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: I measured the displayed distance in the virtual scene: 15 cm.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Did you check the unit?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Yes. I checked the label and saved a screenshot. I did not claim that it was a real measurement.

questions.prompt: What distance was displayed in the virtual scene?
questions.feedback: The student reports a virtual distance of 15 cm.

questions.prompt: What did the student save?
questions.feedback: The student says that a screenshot was saved.

pronunciation.phrase: I checked the label and saved a screenshot.
pronunciation.focus: Contrast the /t/ in checked and the /d/ in saved.

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: At 10:15 I was reading a virtual instrument display.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: What happened then?

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: The screen froze while I was reading the value.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: Did you discover why it froze?

turns.speaker: Lina
turns.text: No, I only recorded what happened in the simulation.

questions.prompt: What was Lina doing when the screen froze?
questions.feedback: Lina was reading the display during the interruption.

questions.prompt: At what time did the interruption happen?
questions.feedback: Lina gives the time as 10:15.

pronunciation.phrase: The screen froze while I was reading the value.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the /w/ in while and distinguish froze from was reading.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: I was updating a virtual measurement table when two entries disappeared.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Did you type replacement values?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: No. I asked for help because I did not know what caused the problem.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: That was sensible. Missing data should not be invented.

questions.prompt: How many table entries disappeared?
questions.feedback: The student says two entries disappeared.

questions.prompt: Did the student invent replacement values?
questions.feedback: The student asked for help instead of inventing data.

pronunciation.phrase: I was updating a virtual measurement table when two entries disappeared.
pronunciation.focus: Practise was updating as a continuing background action and disappeared as the event.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: We have already completed the virtual data table.

turns.speaker: Noura
turns.text: Have you written the conclusion yet?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: No, I haven't written it yet.

turns.speaker: Noura
turns.text: Then our report is not finished, even though the table is complete.

questions.prompt: Which task has already been completed?
questions.feedback: Sam says the virtual data table is complete.

questions.prompt: What has Sam not written yet?
questions.feedback: Sam explicitly says the conclusion is not written yet.

pronunciation.phrase: No, I haven't written it yet.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the contraction haven't and the short final word yet.

turns.speaker: Eva
turns.text: I have just checked the figures in our fictional report.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: When did you draw the graph?

turns.speaker: Eva
turns.text: I drew it on Monday, but I have not checked the axis labels yet.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: So the graph is drawn, but the labels still need checking.

questions.prompt: When did Eva draw the graph?
questions.feedback: Eva uses simple past with the finished time on Monday.

questions.prompt: What still needs checking?
questions.feedback: Eva says that she has not checked the axis labels yet.

pronunciation.phrase: I have just checked the figures in our fictional report.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the reduced have and the consonant sounds in checked.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: In this virtual circuit, resistance stays at 5 ohms.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: When the voltage rises from 5 V to 10 V, current rises from 1 A to 2 A.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Good. That result uses the stated fixed-resistance assumption.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: We should describe these as model values, not measurements from a real circuit.

questions.prompt: What stays constant in the fictional circuit model?
questions.feedback: Resistance is explicitly fixed at 5 ohms.

questions.prompt: What current is shown when voltage is 10 V?
questions.feedback: The dialogue states 2 A at 10 V in the model.

pronunciation.phrase: When the voltage rises from 5 V to 10 V, current rises from 1 A to 2 A.
pronunciation.focus: Pronounce the unit names clearly and emphasize from and to.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: The model starts at zero and moves at 1.5 meters per second.

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: If that speed stays constant, the predicted position after 3 seconds is 4.5 meters.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Is the predicted value a real measurement?

turns.speaker: Noah
turns.text: No. It is a calculation for the model under that condition.

questions.prompt: What speed is assumed in the model?
questions.feedback: The constant-speed assumption is 1.5 meters per second.

questions.prompt: What is the predicted position after 3 seconds?
questions.feedback: The model predicts 4.5 meters after 3 seconds, not a physical measurement.

pronunciation.phrase: If that speed stays constant, the predicted position after 3 seconds is 4.5 meters.
pronunciation.focus: Pause after the if-clause, then make the result clear.

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: On this simulated graph, the horizontal axis is Time in seconds.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: The vertical axis is Position in meters.

turns.speaker: Guide
turns.text: The line rises from zero meters at zero seconds to four meters at two seconds.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: That describes the displayed data. A later position would be a prediction.

questions.prompt: What does the horizontal axis show?
questions.feedback: The guide names time measured in seconds on the horizontal axis.

questions.prompt: What position is shown at two seconds?
questions.feedback: The line ends at 4 meters after 2 seconds in the model.

pronunciation.phrase: The vertical axis is Position in meters.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the stress in vertical and position.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: The virtual temperature display reads 20 degrees Celsius at minute zero.

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.text: At minute four, it reads 24 degrees Celsius.

turns.speaker: Mina
turns.text: The simulated temperature increased by four degrees Celsius.

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.text: We cannot call the value at minute five an observation because it is not shown.

questions.prompt: What is the displayed temperature at minute four?
questions.feedback: The virtual display is 24 °C at minute four.

questions.prompt: What is the increase over the shown interval?
questions.feedback: The increase is 24 minus 20, or 4 degrees Celsius.

pronunciation.phrase: The simulated temperature increased by four degrees Celsius.
pronunciation.focus: Practise increased by rather than increased to when stating a difference.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Your virtual cart table labels Time in seconds and Position in meters.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: It shows a position of 3.0 m at 2 s.

turns.speaker: Tutor
turns.text: Write that as a simulated observation in your report.

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: I will not call it a real laboratory measurement or invent a later data point.

questions.prompt: What position does the virtual table display at 2 s?
questions.feedback: The table displays a simulated position of 3.0 m at 2 seconds.

questions.prompt: How should the student describe this result?
questions.feedback: The tutor asks for a simulated observation, not an actual laboratory measurement.

pronunciation.phrase: It shows a position of 3.0 m at 2 s.
pronunciation.focus: Read each numerical quantity and its unit clearly.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Our group prepared a short explanation of a fictional motion model.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: We described the displayed data first and then the constant-speed assumption.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: For a later time, we wrote a conditional prediction, not an observation.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: We also checked that every numerical value had the correct SI unit.

questions.prompt: What did the group describe first?
questions.feedback: The group described the displayed data before the assumption.

questions.prompt: How did the group treat values at later times?
questions.feedback: They state that later values are conditional predictions, not observations.

pronunciation.phrase: We also checked that every numerical value had the correct SI unit.
pronunciation.focus: Practise the consonants in checked and the stress in numerical.
